decisions.statement: Every name format the index files is judged whatever the change carries.
A format no property names is judged like a format a property names.
A format's judgement is loaded through `format-reaching` rather than again here.
A format's code is loaded from wherever its body sits on disk rather than from the change.
A change writing a format's code anew is refused rather than judged by the body before the change.
What shape a format hands over is read from the body the change leaves rather than from the disk.
A format whose code does not parse is refused for not parsing.
That refusal is read from the body the change leaves rather than from a load.
The fault the parser recovered from is named in that refusal.
A format whose code does not parse is judged for nothing else.
A format exports one name bound to `matching` of a shape written out.
A shape reached through a name is no shape written out.
The name a format exports is the name its slug answers to.
A shape with the `g` flag is refused.
A shape with `g` keeps a `lastIndex` between asks and so answers one name differently.
A format that fails is named in a refusal of its own.
A format that fails where the change names an edit at its code is refused as written.
A refusal over code the change names no edit at says the change did not write what failed.
The names a shape lets through are not judged here.
Whether two formats have one shape is not judged here.

definition: the check refusing a name format not judging by one shape its own code hands over
